t: Count Triplets with Even XOR Set Bits I
o: With arrays of size ≤ 100, brute force over all triples is at most 1e6 operations — trivially fast. The XOR parity insight gives an O(n) counting alternative: XOR has an even number of set bits iff the parities of popcounts of the three operands sum to an even number, i.e., an even count of the three parities are odd.
k: Precompute parity of popcount per element; count even/odd buckets per array.

a.i: Triple loop computing bin(x).count('1') % 2 == 0 on the XOR; sizes guarantee ≤ 1e6 iterations.
s: Loop i, j, k over a, b, c.

a.i: Only the popcount parity of each element matters. Bucket each array into even/odd parity counts and combine: the XOR parity is even exactly when 0 or 2 of the three parities are odd.
s: Compute (ea, oa), (eb, ob), (ec, oc) via popcount parity.
a.t: O(n) — one parity pass per array

w: Brute force is perfectly fine at these constraints; mention the parity trick as the elegant follow-up (it scales to 1e5-sized arrays instantly). Pitfall: remember 0 has popcount 0 (even). Verify example 2: parities yield 4 as required.
